overview.heading: Overview
overview.content: Discrimination RPG is an interactive text-based role-playing game designed to immerse players in real-world social scenarios involving discrimination, bias, and difficult decision-making.

purpose.heading: Purpose
purpose.content: The project was built to educate players on the subtle and overt forms of discrimination that individuals experience in everyday environments. By placing players directly into branching storylines, the game aims to build empathy, highlight systemic inequities, and spark meaningful reflection. It also served as a way to combine storytelling with software development, demonstrating how interactive media can explore important social issues.

steps.title: Branching Narrative Scenarios
steps.description: Players explore multiple storylines with different outcomes based on their decisions, allowing each playthrough to reveal new perspectives on discrimination and race-related challenges.

steps.title: Mental Health & Food Resource System
steps.description: A lightweight resource-management mechanic tracks mental health and food levels, affecting available choices and long-term outcomes, adding depth and realism to the gameplay experience.

steps.title: Explorable Locations
steps.description: Players can visit various in-game locations, each offering unique events, challenges, and conversations that shape the narrative and player progression.

steps.title: User Input Handling & State Management
steps.description: Robust input validation ensures smooth gameplay while internal state-tracking maintains player stats, choices, and scenario transitions.
